title: The Door With a Condition
concept: A half-open Gate with a face stands for the Fairbanks Assembly's August request to pause new commercial data centers until standards exist. The film shows that the October 6th vote did not decide the question, that the pause is a door with a condition rather than a no, and that a University of Alaska Fairbanks guide, Computing in Place, hands out questions while the one data center bill that moved stalled in the House, so the open question is who writes the rules. A gold question token changes state across the film and the blank STANDARDS sheet is the unpaid promise.

fingerprint.palette: bright pearl fog daylight, warm cranberry gate, golden larch token, teal-black shadow, navy ink stamp
fingerprint.light_story: fog thickening through the Test, thinning at the turn, closing in at the button
fingerprint.metaphor: a gate with a condition on its plate, waiting for a hand to write the rule

palette: bright pearl fog daylight, warm cranberry gate, golden larch token, teal-black shadow, navy ink stamp
divergence_note: 10-11 opened on first-light rose tundra with a medicine crate, 10-10 was a night parking lot under sodium lamps and 10-09 a dusk utility yard. This film opens in pearl daylight ice fog on a cranberry Gate that is the seam between a YES side and a NO side, moves through a plan-view gym floor of chairs, a count table, a map, a hallway and a guide desk, and ends on a thin loop to the fog. The hero is a conditional rule rather than a machine or an object being carried, the opening is a split frame rather than a centred portrait, and its palette is pearl, cranberry and larch gold, none of which the last three decks used. The honest overlaps are daylight and a pale snow world, which 10-11 also had, so the break comes from the hue family and the split composition.

treatment.winner: The Dramatist's half-open Gate and its Padlock scene, with the Comedian's polite no and waiting machine, the Explainer's chair grid and four dials, and the Enthusiast's two apertures as the turn.
treatment.why: All four pitches cast the Gate as hero and the QuestionToken as throughline, so the synthesis took each room's strongest fair beat.

angle.thesis: Fairbanks didn't settle data centers on October 6th, it asked for rules first, and the rules are the one thing nobody has written yet, which is the part Alaska can still win by writing.
angle.falsifier: If voters were asked a data center question and answered it, or the winners' verified positions show they ran on the pause, or the Assembly could impose the pause itself, or the request had no end condition, the thesis is false. The claims show none of those: turnout 20.95 percent, an unofficial 217-vote margin over a challenger who took no position, a request only the Legislature can grant, and a pause that ends when standards exist.
supporting_facts: c4 about one in five borough voters cast a ballot
c1 Howell won by an unofficial 217, over Ramirez who couldn't say yay or nay without more studies (c8)
c5 and c6 the Assembly's August request is a request to Juneau that pauses new commercial data centers until standards exist
c9 a data center bill passed the Senate 14-5 and the House never took it up
c13 and c14 UAF's guide hands out questions, and says a small hospital or tribal facility raises different questions from a hyperscale one
angle.counterpoint: A pause until standards exist, with nobody drafting standards, works as a no in practice, and the winning incumbent LaJiness's flat 'not good for any community' (c7) is the honest version of it. Waiting for a mandate is itself a choice that favors whoever builds first. The film draws that case at full strength as its Act 3 test, then answers it with the conditional text of the request, the scale distinction and the Senate majority.

runner_ups.lost_because: Pure no-mandate framing is a correction, and left the viewer with nothing to want. Its turnout and margin scenes, the August-before-October timeline and its closing question are kept.
The false-binary line is kept as the hook, but alone it had no object to hold.
Led with upside the claims can't carry (no standards are on the way). Its hospital-scale versus hyperscale upside is kept as the turn.

angle.cross_challenge: All three analysts independently refused the brief's overstatement that three winners back a pause and that Howell wanted more analysis, neither of which is in the claims. Synthesis builds on the unofficial count, the conditional request and the guide's questions only.
writer_guardrails: Never say certified or final, every count is unofficial
The 6-1 was the whole 2027 priorities package, say request to Juneau
No position for Howell or Crass, none is in the claims
Leaders's moratorium support is a paraphrase, never quoted
No Senate bill number or sponsor
Guide is mid-October or this month, never released October 14th
Guide questions are as UAF summarizes, the no-figures claim covers the release and record only
